sheet-34-1.description: Lower half of sheet 34 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today the bay side of central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the bay at the left and Arctic Avenue at the right edge. It covers the blocks between Hudson Avenue, Railroad Avenue and Arctic Avenue, crossed by West Taylor, West Rio Grande and West Hand Avenues. West of Hudson Avenue are the eastern ends of blocks 44 and 36, between Hudson and Railroad Avenues blocks 45 and 37, and between Railroad Avenue and Arctic Avenue the narrow blocks 166 and 167, with block 168 at the top and 165 at the foot. Almost the whole area is laid out in numbered lots but still vacant: only a few dwellings stand on it, among them a cottage named Meadow View, a pair of bungalows and two or three small houses near Railroad Avenue. A six-inch water pipe is drawn in West Rio Grande Avenue at Hudson Avenue and at Arctic Avenue. Railroad Avenue, 80 feet wide, is the line of today's Park Boulevard. The sheet is divided by a heavy line from the upper half, which shows the blocks further west on Grassy Sound at a different position on the page.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today Park Boulevard; West Rio Grande Avenue is today Rio Grande Avenue.
Cottage Meadow View in block 44 on West Taylor Avenue.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) Hudson Av, Railroad Av (today Park Blvd) and Arctic Av x W Taylor, W Rio Grande, W Hand; part 2 (upper) Susquehanna Av and Grassy Sound creek x the same avenues, further west (helmert on Susquehanna).

sheet-34-2.description: Upper half of sheet 34 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the lower half by a heavy line. It shows the western edge of the town on Grassy Sound, the bay side of today's Wildwood, between West Taylor Avenue at the top and West Hand Avenue at the foot, with Susquehanna Avenue running down the middle. A tidal creek of Grassy Sound, coloured blue, winds through the blocks west of Susquehanna Avenue and cuts off their western lots; the sound itself fills the left margin. West Rio Grande Avenue leaves the town westward across the water on a wooden bridge marked Turnpike, with a note that boat houses lie about 500 feet away on a detached sheet, number 45. The blocks (43, 44, 35 1/2 and 36, with the edges of 52, 53 and 28 1/2, 29 beyond the avenues) are laid out in numbered lots but nearly empty. The only large building is the Rio Grand Inn on West Rio Grande Avenue near the creek, with a store and small outbuildings at the bridge end; a cottage named Maple Shade stands near the east edge of block 44. A compass rose is drawn in the open sound. The blocks east of the right edge continue in the lower half of the sheet, beyond Hudson Avenue.
notes: Placed with a helmert transformation from the three Susquehanna Avenue junctions only (one line of control); low to medium confidence away from Susquehanna Avenue.
The wooden bridge on West Rio Grande Avenue is lettered (Turnpike); the creek shore has since been filled and rebuilt.
Rio Grand Inn is lettered without the final e.

Map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) Hudson Av, Railroad Av (today Park Blvd) and Arctic Av x W Taylor, W Rio Grande, W Hand; part 2 (upper) Susquehanna Av and Grassy Sound creek x the same avenues, further west (helmert on Susquehanna).

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from Arctic Avenue at the left edge across Holly Beach Avenue to about half way towards Pacific Avenue, between West and East Hand Avenue at the top and West and East Cresse Avenue at the foot. Holly Beach Avenue runs down the middle 100 to 110 feet wide with the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (lettered W. J. & S. R. R.) in it; a section house stands beside the tracks near Bennett Avenue. The blocks are laid out in lots numbered from 1 to 30 with block numbers 31, 24, 17 and 10 on the west side and 32, 25, 18 and 11 on the east. Building is sparse: scattered frame dwellings, mostly of one and two storeys, a few larger houses with outbuildings, a boarding house and servants' quarters on West Leaming and Bennett Avenues, a greenhouse (hot house) and a water pipe in each cross avenue (six inch, with four inch near Hand Avenue). Many blocks, notably those between Bennett and Hildreth Avenues, are empty. A compass rose is drawn at the top. Adjoining sheets are 37 above, 31 and 32 below and 36 to the east.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn Arctic Avenue centre plus 685 ft at the atlas scale, because the railroad fills the street and its drawn width (100 to 110 ft) differs from today's 72 ft right-of-way.
Philadelphia Avenue is lettered at the foot of the sheet beside the tracks; modern name not checked.
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.

Map, 50 ft. Arctic Av (left edge) across Holly Beach Av (railroad; today New Jersey Av) to half way to Pacific; W/E Hand, Leaming, Bennett, Hildreth, Cresse Avs. NJ junctions hand-picked (Arctic + 685 ft). Holly Beach Av lettered Philadelphia Av. south of Cresse.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the ground from half a block west of Pacific Avenue across Pacific Avenue to the boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean, between East Hand Avenue at the top and East Cresse Avenue at the foot. Blocks 32, 25, 18 and 11 lie west of Pacific Avenue and 33, 26, 19 and 12 east of it, each laid out in narrow lots numbered up to 30. The east blocks are mostly empty. Buildings are scattered frame dwellings and cottages, some on piles near the shore, a boarding house with a water tank, the Harvey and the Renovo, a bath house, and the United States Life Saving Station with its boat house and living quarters on East Leaming Avenue at Pacific Avenue. Approaches to the boardwalk are shown dashed at the ends of the avenues, and the boardwalk and ocean edge run down the right margin with a yellow hatched strip for the beach. At the foot the shoreline cuts in, with open water lettered Atlantic Ocean and a shelter at the boardwalk. A compass rose is drawn at the top left. Adjoining sheets are 38 above, 32 below and 35 to the west.
notes: The boardwalk lies on the line of today's Atlantic Avenue; the detector places Atlantic Avenue junctions about 35 ft beyond the drawn ocean-side block line.
Atlantic Avenue / East Cresse Avenue falls in the ocean notch at the foot of the sheet and was not detected.
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.
Map, 50 ft. Half block west of Pacific Av across Pacific to the boardwalk (on today's Atlantic Av line); E Hand, Leaming, Bennett, Hildreth, Cresse Avs.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the blocks from Arctic Avenue at the left edge across Holly Beach Avenue, which runs down the middle of the sheet 100 to 110 feet wide and carries the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (lettered W. J. & S. R. R.) with sidings, to half way towards Pacific Avenue. The cross streets are West and East Burk, Andrews, Taylor, Rio Grande and Hand Avenues, each with a four-inch water pipe. The railroad passenger depot, with a news stand, stands in Holly Beach Avenue between Andrews and Taylor Avenues, and the old freight depot beside the tracks south of Taylor Avenue. The blocks are closely built with frame dwellings of one to three storeys, many of them cottages and boarding houses, with stores along the avenues near the station: a bake shop with oven on East Burk Avenue, an insurance office, an office and dwelling, the New Centre House on West Taylor Avenue, the Brunswick Inn on East Rio Grande Avenue and a bath house and shed nearby. Lot numbers and street numbers are given throughout, and fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked. A compass rose is drawn in Holly Beach Avenue at Burk Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheet 45 beyond Arctic Avenue, 39 to the north, 38 towards the ocean and 35 to the south.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn Arctic Avenue centre plus 685 ft at the atlas scale, because the railroad fills the street and its drawn width (100 to 110 ft) differs from today's 72 ft right-of-way.
West and East Rio Grande Avenue are today Rio Grande Avenue.
Passenger depot of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad in Holly Beach Avenue between Andrews and Taylor Avenues; old freight depot south of Taylor Avenue.

Map, 50 ft. Arctic Av (left edge) across Holly Beach Av (railroad, passenger depot; today New Jersey Av) to half way to Pacific; W/E Burk, Andrews, Taylor, Rio Grande, Hand Avs. NJ junctions hand-picked (Arctic + 685 ft).

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach, today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the ocean side of the town from half way between Holly Beach and Pacific Avenues across Pacific Avenue to the boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean at the right edge, between East Burk Avenue at the top and East Hand Avenue at the foot (East Andrews, East Taylor and East Rio Grande Avenues between). This is the business and resort centre of Holly Beach. On Pacific Avenue stand the Bourse Building with stores and an insurance office, the Hotel Pacific, a post office, a private hospital, boarding houses, the Philadelphia House with saloon and summer garden, the Centre House, a bakery, an automobile garage and many stores with dwellings above. The public school, heated by steam and lit by gas, is at East Burk Avenue on the left. Along the boardwalk the blocks end in bathing establishments built on piles, reached by approaches from each avenue: the Central Baths and the Majestic Baths at Burk Avenue, Butts Bath House at Andrews Avenue, and at Rio Grande Avenue the Gladstone with its dining room and a wooden platform level with the boardwalk, and a shooting gallery. Beyond the boardwalk the beach is hatched yellow and the ocean coloured blue, with a pavilion on piles at Taylor Avenue. C. A. Norton, contractor, has storage sheds on East Rio Grande Avenue. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: The boardwalk (lettered Board Walk) runs where Atlantic Avenue is today: the ocean-side block line on this sheet is today's west line of Atlantic Avenue, and the detector placed the Atlantic Avenue junctions 35 ft beyond it.
East Rio Grande Avenue is today Rio Grande Avenue.
Bathing houses on piles: Central Baths, The Majestic Baths, Butts Bath House, the Gladstone.
Map, 50 ft. Pilot. Half block west of Pacific Av across Pacific to the boardwalk (today's Atlantic Av line; detector places Atlantic 35 ft beyond the block line); E Burk to E Hand Av.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from Arctic Avenue at the left edge across Holly Beach Avenue to about half way towards Pacific Avenue, between West and East Roberts Avenue at the top and West and East Burk Avenue at the foot. Holly Beach Avenue is wide and carries the main line and sidings of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (W. J. & S. R. R.), which curves across the street. Beside the tracks stand a store house, a fish platform, an ice house, the railroad's iron-clad freight house and an open platform. The blocks are numbered 101, 92, 83 and 74 on the west and 102, 93, 84 and 75 on the east. Houses are mostly small frame dwellings, with bait boxes behind the fish platform. South of Davis Avenue the sheet is industrial: a livery, a wagon works, the Diamond and Company lumber yard with lumber sheds, F. E. Smith, contractor, with a planing mill, the Woodruff and Laning ice plant and J. Davis ice cream factory, the Holly Beach Cold Storage Company, and a boat builder. A compass rose is drawn in Holly Beach Avenue. Adjoining sheets are 41 above, 37 below and 40 to the east.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn Arctic Avenue centre plus 685 ft at the atlas scale, because the railroad fills the street and its drawn width (100 to 110 ft) differs from today's 72 ft right-of-way. On this sheet the railroad curves across the street; the same rule was used.
Freight house of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad and several lumber yards and an ice plant stand beside the tracks.
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.
Map, 50 ft. Arctic Av across Holly Beach Av (railroad, curve) to half way to Pacific; W/E Roberts, Baker, Montgomery, Davis, Burk Avs. NJ junctions hand-picked (Arctic + 685 ft).

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the ground from half a block west of Pacific Avenue across Pacific Avenue to the boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean, between East Roberts Avenue at the top and East Burk Avenue at the foot. Blocks 102, 93, 84 and 75 lie west of Pacific Avenue and 103, 94, 85 and 76 east of it. The blocks near Pacific Avenue are closely built with frame dwellings and boarding houses and several named buildings: the Hollywood M. E. Church, the Westminster, Seaside Apartments, Marine Cottage, Dorothy L. Cottage, Hotel Dorsey, Holly Beach City Hall with the fire company (Fire Co. No. 1), Beachwood House, the Swedish Mission Church, Somerset Apartments, the First Presbyterian Church and the Havilla. A Blk Sm (blacksmith) shop is marked in green. Toward the boardwalk the lots are mostly empty. Approaches to the boardwalk are dashed at the ends of the avenues, and the boardwalk with the Atlantic Ocean runs down the right margin. A compass rose is drawn at the top. Adjoining sheets are 42 above, 38 below and 39 to the west.
notes: The boardwalk lies on the line of today's Atlantic Avenue.
Holly Beach City Hall, with the Fire Co. No. 1 quarters, stands at Pacific Avenue and East Montgomery Avenue.
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.
Map, 50 ft. Half block west of Pacific Av across Pacific to the ocean side; E Roberts, Baker, Montgomery, Davis, Burk Avs.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from Arctic Avenue at the left edge across Holly Beach Avenue to about half way towards Pacific Avenue, between West and East Garfield Avenue at the top and West and East Roberts Avenue at the foot. Holly Beach Avenue carries the tracks of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (W. J. & S. R. R.), which swing east of the street centre towards the bottom. The blocks are numbered 134, 126, 118 and 110 on the west and 135, 127, 119 and 111 on the east. The top left block holds the Chas. H. Clouting Co. lumber yard with sheds and a planing mill and the W. H. Austin and Co. coal and wood yard. East of the tracks at Spicer and Spencer Avenues stand The West Jersey Electric Co., a power house with direct-current generators, alternators, arc dynamos and exciters, a wooden tank, a coal bin, a storage of material and the iron-clad car barn. Other buildings are frame dwellings, a storage house, an M. E. Church (Colored) on East Youngs Avenue and the Lillian. The west side beyond the lumber yard is thinly built. A compass rose is drawn at the top left. Adjoining sheets are 43 above, 39 below and 42 to the east.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn Arctic Avenue centre plus 685 ft at the atlas scale, because the railroad fills the street and its drawn width (100 to 110 ft) differs from today's 72 ft right-of-way.

Arctic Avenue / West Garfield Avenue is not drawn at the sheet edge; the East Garfield and New Jersey Avenue point was hand-picked from the drawn street edges (centre at the middle of the street and its water pipe).
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.

Map, 50 ft. Arctic Av across Holly Beach Av (railroad) to half way to Pacific; W/E Garfield, Spicer, Spencer, Youngs, Roberts Avs. NJ junctions hand-picked (Arctic + 685 ft). Arctic / W Garfield not drawn.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach (New Jersey Coast volume 4), today central Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It covers the ground from half a block west of Pacific Avenue across Pacific Avenue to the boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean, between East Garfield Avenue at the top and East Roberts Avenue at the foot. Blocks 135, 127, 119 and 111 lie west of Pacific Avenue and 136, 128, 120 and 112 east of it. Along Pacific Avenue stand dwellings and boarding houses, with St. Ann R. C. Church, the Melrose, Elston Boarding, Rowland Hall, the Lansdowne, Franklin Ho., an undertaker, the Universal and, on the east side, St. Charles. On the boardwalk the Philadelphia Building (with moving pictures on piles) and the Washington Building, the Washington Bath Houses and its annex stand on piles at the shore, with a public pavilion and an office on piles. Most of the east blocks are empty lots. Dashed approaches to the boardwalk end each avenue, and the boardwalk and ocean run down the right margin. A compass rose is drawn at the top. Adjoining sheets are 44 above, 40 below and 41 to the west.
notes: The boardwalk lies on the line of today's Atlantic Avenue.
The Philadelphia Building and the Washington Building and bath houses stand on piles on the ocean side of the boardwalk.
Names, building labels and the readings were taken from the 1600 px overview with spot checks on full-resolution crops; small lettering may be misread.
Map, 50 ft. Half block west of Pacific Av across Pacific to the ocean side; E Garfield, Spicer, Spencer, Youngs, Roberts Avs.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach, at the north end of the town towards Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the bay side is at the top. Arctic Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and Holly Beach Avenue, here 120 feet wide with four railroad tracks, crosses the middle; the cross streets are West and East Garfield, Lincoln and Schellenger Avenues and, at the right, West and East Cedar Avenue, which narrows between converging lines towards Arctic Avenue, where Schellenger Avenue opens out to 102 feet. Philadelphia Avenue is lettered at the right beyond Holly Beach Avenue. Between Arctic and Holly Beach Avenues is the town's industrial strip: the works of the Wildwood, Anglesea and Holly Beach Gas Company with gasometer, purifying house, engine room and generator house, oil tanks of the Standard Oil Company, the Seaboard Artificial Stone Company, a pipe shop, the J. H. Coombs Lumber Company with lumber sheds, carpenter shop and an office and hardware store, a blacksmith, a pool room, The Grand Laundry Company and old junk yards. South of Holly Beach Avenue the blocks hold frame dwellings and boarding houses, a carpenter shop, a sign painter, a plumber and a livery stable. Across the top are the first lots of blocks 177 and 178 north of Arctic Avenue. Galvanized iron water pipes run in Cedar Avenue.
notes: Holly Beach Avenue is today New Jersey Avenue; its junctions were hand-picked as the drawn Arctic Avenue centre plus 685 ft at the atlas scale (railroad fills the 120 ft street).
Arctic Avenue / West Schellenger Avenue hand-picked from the west line of Schellenger Avenue, which widens to 102 ft at Arctic Avenue.
Cedar Avenue does not meet Arctic or New Jersey Avenue in today's street network; Philadelphia Avenue is not in today's network.
Gas works of the Wildwood, Anglesea and Holly Beach Gas Co.; man on duty nights, city water.
Map, 50 ft, turned (bay at top). Arctic Av and Holly Beach Av (120 ft, railroad; today New Jersey Av) x Garfield, Lincoln, Schellenger, Cedar Avs; gas works, lumber yard. NJ junctions hand-picked.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 of the 1909 Sanborn survey of Holly Beach, the north end of the resort's ocean front towards Wildwood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the ocean is at the foot. Pacific Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet and Atlantic Avenue the lower part, with East Garfield, East Lincoln, East Schellenger and East Cedar Avenues running down the page; above Pacific Avenue are the ends of blocks 143, 150 and 157 towards Holly Beach Avenue. The blocks are filled with hotels, boarding houses and cottages: The Berwind, The Strand, The Brighton, the Leigh Apartments and The Eleanor north of Pacific Avenue, and south of it The Colonial, the Republican Club, Hotel Donalan, Hotel Grenoble, Pinker's Hotel with a beer garden, the Oaklyn, Storch's Cottage, Hotel Thelma, The Lyndhurst, the Imperial, the Majestic, the Edgewater and The Ruric with a summer pavilion. A bake house, a warehouse and stores stand on Pacific Avenue, and The Star moving pictures on East Garfield Avenue. Beyond Atlantic Avenue the boardwalk curves along the shore, and between them, on piles, are Sweet's Up to Date Bath Houses, Blaker's Baths and Blaker's Theater, a bath office and pavilion, moving picture houses, an auction store, a photograph gallery and other small shops facing the boardwalk, with another pavilion at the foot. The Atlantic Ocean is coloured blue along the lower left. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: Atlantic Avenue is drawn as a 50 ft street on this sheet; further south (sheet 38) the boardwalk runs on its line.
Boardwalk lettered Board Walk; amusements on piles: Sweet's Up to Date Bath Houses, Blaker's Baths, Blaker's Theater.
Map, 50 ft, turned (ocean at foot). Pacific and Atlantic Avs x E Garfield, Lincoln, Schellenger, Cedar; boardwalk, baths and theatre on piles.
